feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear domain focus and solid public-sector progression. It reads professionally and shows impact, but it is somewhat dense, repetitive across sections, and could sharpen results with more outcome-focused metrics.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression consistently support a senior digital platform/communications leadership profile.  
- Strong credibility: long tenure at one organization with steady advancement, relevant technical breadth, and concrete scale indicators like “10,000+ page website” and “3.5 million annual page views.”  
- Good scope of expertise: combines strategy, governance, analytics, CMS/platform work, multimedia, and AI-enabled search in a way that feels current and differentiated.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve structure and scannability.  
- Add clearer outcomes: several bullets describe responsibilities well but need stronger business/user results (e.g., engagement lift, efficiency gains, adoption, cost savings, campaign performance).  
- Fix style consistency: use parallel bullet formatting throughout; some entries are full paragraphs with inline dashes. Minor stylistic inconsistencies include “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” “social, and multimedia” (remove comma), and mixed capitalization/formatting in the footer. No major misspellings or grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it is slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience bullets.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one sharper value proposition and foreground the most relevant niche: public-sector digital modernization at enterprise scale.
- Add 1–2 concrete scope signals already supported elsewhere, such as enterprise web modernization, analytics/governance, and multi-channel content operations.
- Replace the generic “building the platforms” phrasing with more direct action verbs like “leading,” “modernizing,” or “scaling.”
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web platforms, governance models, analytics infrastructure, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Leads digital transformation across editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep it brief here.
- The subtitle already signals leadership, so avoid repeating “digital leader” too heavily elsewhere.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline and recent roles, but the section is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing higher-level leadership strengths will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use more concise, executive-level labels and reduce “operations” repetition.
- Prioritize the most marketable recent strengths: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation, and public-sector communications.
- Consider rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy and communications leadership • Multimedia production and livestream delivery
- Replace “Multi-channel communications operations” with “communications leadership” or drop it if space is tight.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” overlaps with Topline Skills and Recent Projects.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” and analytics/governance themes are already well covered elsewhere.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding parallel structure will improve scanability and impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and format each item as: project name + concise outcome-focused description.
- Tighten wording and use parallel verbs: “Created,” “Built,” “Developed,” “Launched.” Example: “Created an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat.”
- Replace vague phrases with sharper ones: “continued campaign growth” → “future campaign expansion”; “connected to the main site” → “integrated with the main site.”
- Standardize style and punctuation; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency and readability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with recent NACo roles; keep this section brief and project-specific to avoid repeating Work Experience.
- “Editorial storytelling” and “production and distribution” echo existing skills sections; emphasize distinct deliverables or outcomes instead.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Core Competencies

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consulting impact, platform modernization, and the AI/search work.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, and communications operations for member-facing campaigns and web properties.”
- Replace generic verbs (“consult,” “advise,” “deliver”) with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Redesigned workflows…,” “Built modular Drupal campaign experiences…,” “Led AI-enabled search initiative…”
- Consolidate into 3–4 bullets, e.g.:
- Improved digital governance, workflows, and analytics for coordinated cross-channel communications.
- Built Drupal campaign/microsite experiences with modular content, downloadable toolkits, and front-end enhancements for public-facing properties.
- Led AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content model, and discovery UX.
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages, publishing teams supported, campaign launches, search accuracy gains, engagement/conversion improvements, or time saved.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” and “Drupal/web improvement” repeat the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize consultant-level scope and new initiatives.
- Microsite and AI-search details also appear in Recent Projects; keep this item higher-level.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It should be tightened to emphasize the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget.”
- Prioritize the standout achievements and lead with metrics: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make impact more explicit: add results for the studio and analytics work if available (e.g., reduced vendor spend, faster reporting, increased production volume, improved campaign performance).
- Condense channel oversight into one line and use stronger verbs: “Oversaw newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social channels serving thousands of followers.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version higher-level.
- Video-program expansion also appears in earlier roles; focus here on building the in-house studio and organizational capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story and good channel breadth, but the item reads generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Tighten it around execution leadership, editorial systems, and any measurable audience/output growth.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and function: “Directed day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social, and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy publishing across NACo.”
- Make bullets more outcome-led and parallel:
- Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Built stronger editorial planning across communications, advocacy, and program teams to improve alignment and publishing cadence.
- Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve consistency, speed, and cross-team coordination.
- If possible, add metrics: newsletter open/click rates, video frequency/views, publishing volume, or turnaround-time improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video as a recurring channel” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; keep this version focused on scaling/operationalizing it.
- “Improved workflows/governance” overlaps with the 2022–2024 role; avoid broad governance language here.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies and reads generic rather than differentiated. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and audience/governance strengths not already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Use “operations” or “publishing standards” instead of “systems” to avoid repeating “editorial systems” from Core Competencies.
- Change “messaging” to “communications” for a more senior, strategic tone.
- Change “planning” to “strategy” to better match director/consultant-level positioning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” is also close to “Multi-channel communications operations”; vary the wording to avoid echo.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it’s too tool-heavy and overlaps with the more detailed “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution strengths, not exhaustive software listing.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a tool list to a capability-led line, with the most relevant/recent strengths first.
- Cut lower-priority or older-feeling items here (e.g., jQuery) unless central to target roles.
- Suggested rewrite: Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end web implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills broader and let Technical + IT hold the full tool inventory.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies, so consider keeping it in only one place unless it’s a signature differentiator.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

- Power BI

Suggested edit

- KPI design and executive reporting

- “Leadership reporting” overlaps with “analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies; “executive reporting” is cleaner and more distinct.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize delivery capability and recent leadership-level multimedia work rather than tool-level detail.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production & Live Event Operations**

- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production  
- Livestream and hybrid event production  
- In-house studio and control-room operations  
- PTZ camera direction and multi-camera workflows
- If possible, add scale/context elsewhere on the CV rather than here (e.g., studio built, recurring advocacy series, event support volume).
- Keep phrasing noun-based and parallel; avoid mixing broad categories with specific hardware unless all bullets are similarly scoped.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” / “multimedia production” already appears in Core Competencies; use this section to be more specific, not repetitive.
- “Studio operations” and tool details also overlap with “Multimedia & Creative Tools”; avoid turning this into another software list.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add level/context or be tightened to emphasize the most credible, recent platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by depth/relevance: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider signaling proficiency: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add a light qualifier for impact: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; 3.5M annual page views)** to anchor your strongest platform cred.
- Consider renaming the heading to be more execution-focused: **CMS & Web Platform Administration** or **CMS Platforms**
- Keep only platforms you can defend with recent hands-on use; if GitHub Pages was minor, remove it to sharpen the list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially overlaps with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider merging or differentiating one section by adding proficiency/context.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid repeating it elsewhere without new detail.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical range, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools most relevant to recent work and modernize the phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End & Technical Implementation
- Replace with: HTML/CSS • JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the rest of the CV uses version-specific naming; it feels dated.
- If accurate, add one impact-oriented qualifier in nearby experience instead of here, e.g., “used for Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, workflow automation, and lightweight edge functions.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears under Topline Skills; keep the fuller list in one place and shorten the other.
- jQuery may signal older implementation work; keep it only if still actively used in recent Drupal projects.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since workflow automation already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more systems-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize categories and strongest tools: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello | Collaboration: Slack • Microsoft Teams”
- Consider dropping Basecamp unless it was used recently or materially; it feels older/less central than the others.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier to show application, e.g. “workflow automation, intake tracking, editorial planning, cross-team coordination.”
- Order by relevance to recent work and impact: automation/build tools first, then project management, then collaboration tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” is already stated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating that phrase verbatim here.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp overlap as project-management tools; listing all four may feel redundant unless each was meaningfully used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of email/engagement leadership. Because email operations already appear in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and emphasize enterprise-grade systems over basic tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/seniority: “Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp”
- If accurate, add functional scope instead of only product names: “Higher Logic (member email/community) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey orchestration/segmentation) • Mailchimp”
- Keep naming consistent and shorter: consider “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys” rather than the slash format.
- If one platform was primary in the 2022–present roles, place it first and consider dropping the least relevant tool to tighten focus.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with repeated “email newsletters” and “digital communications channels” in work experience; avoid expanding into responsibilities here.
- Mailchimp may feel less strategic than the other two unless it was used recently or materially.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and repeats analytics platforms already evidenced in the recent Director role. This item should be tightened and reframed to emphasize capability breadth, not duplicate the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Reporting & Optimization**
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Tag Manager • KPI reporting • SEO analysis • A/B testing**
- Replace vague **Dashboarding** with **KPI reporting** or **executive reporting** for clearer business value.
- If truthful, add one higher-signal specialty over a generic term, e.g. **measurement strategy**, **conversion analysis**, or **behavior analytics**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly identical to **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping detail in only one place.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already called out in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating the exact same phrasing elsewhere.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and tie it to “firsts,” production volume, or workflow improvements.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout and concrete contributions: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add measurable outputs if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event count, weekly video cadence, audience growth, or production turnaround improvements.
- Tighten the leadership phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “supervised/mentored a digital media associate” if accurate.
- Possible version: “Promoted across two roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, while mentoring a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/producing the format, not expanding it.
- “Strengthening workflows” is repeated elsewhere; specify what changed or cut it here.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and underplays the most distinctive achievement: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since later roles already cover broad digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation, research support, and first-of-its-kind multimedia work.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to lead with the standout outcome: “Supported innovation and policy research initiatives for NACo programs while expanding the organization’s early digital content capabilities.”
- Add a sharper second sentence: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with specifics such as “produced multimedia and digital content assets for program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of episodes launched, audiences served, or programs/projects supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production/multimedia” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate leadership; frame this as a foundational role that set up later digital/media progression.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads more like a mixed tools/functions list than a sharp technical skills entry. It also overlaps heavily with stronger, more recent multimedia leadership evidence elsewhere in the CV.

Suggested edit:
- Rename and tighten to emphasize software first: **Creative & Production Tools: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator**
